items.text: A lot of it was recorded late at night, once the voices had warmed up or the band had loosened up at its cocktail hour.
items.why: Recording, Christopher Bear: 'A lot of the stuff we'd end up recording was really late at night, after voices had really warmed up, or after properly loosening up at our religious cocktail hour'.

items.text: 5 September 2006
items.why: Infobox: 'Released: September 5, 2006'.

items.text: July 2006, at Ed Droste's mother's house on Cape Cod
items.why: Recording: 'began recording at Ed Droste's mother's house on Cape Cod in July 2006' (Lead: the 'majority of recording' took place there).

items.text: Chris Taylor
items.why: Infobox: 'Producer: Chris Taylor'.

items.text: Warp
items.why: Infobox: 'Label: Warp'.

items.text: Christopher Bear (drums, vocals, xylophone, lap steel, glockenspiel), Edward Droste (vocals, keyboard, autoharp, guitar), Daniel Rossen (vocals, guitars, banjo, piano, autoharp), Chris Taylor (clarinet, flute, saxophone, vocals, keyboard, bass, electronics and treatments)
items.why: Band section lists these four with these instruments.

items.text: Grizzly Bear was a solo name for vocalist Ed Droste, and Horn of Plenty, released in 2004, was a solo effort.
items.why: Background: 'release of Horn of Plenty in 2004, Grizzly Bear expanded from being the solo moniker for vocalist Ed Droste'; Recording: 'Horn of Plenty was a solo effort by Droste'.

items.text: After that, the name grew into a full group, with Horn of Plenty collaborator Christopher Bear, Chris Taylor and Daniel Rossen joining Droste.
items.why: Background: 'expanded ... into a full band, with the addition of Horn of Plenty collaborator Christopher Bear, ... Chris Taylor, and ... Daniel Rossen'.

items.text: Christopher Bear said that putting a band together for live shows changed the dynamics and instruments, and helped them find a band sound.
items.why: Background: 'Getting together the band for the live show changed things quite a bit, in terms of dynamics and instrumentation used' is supported, but Bear credits the band sound to the Horn of Plenty songs being 'simple and open ended so it left a lot of room for interpretation, which ... allowed us to get a band sound happening'; the notes move that cause onto forming the band.

items.text: Unlike Horn of Plenty, every member of the four-piece had a hand in writing and producing this record.
items.why: Recording: 'As Horn of Plenty was a solo effort by Droste, this record ... features all members contributing to the writing and production of the album'.

items.text: After about a month of basic tracking, each member added overdubs on their own, and some of them took a long time.
items.why: Recording: 'Following a month of initial tracking, each band member added individual overdubs at a later date'; 'a lot of those sounds were very time intensive'.

items.text: Christopher Bear said some of those parts would have been hard with everyone in the room, or with the meter running at a studio.
items.why: Recording: 'I couldn't imagine doing some of those things with everyone around, or feeling like you're on the clock at a studio'.

items.text: Daniel Rossen's arrival gave the band two main songwriters, and Christopher Bear said the mix of four members' ideas changed the sound most.
items.why: Writing: 'The addition of ... Daniel Rossen ... resulted in two primary songwriters'; Bear: 'having four people with different ideas and strengths has changed our sound the most'.

items.text: Droste and Chris Taylor said the lyrics have no real theme, but the album is about the band learning to work together while recording in that house.
items.why: Writing: 'There is not really a theme with the lyrics but the theme of the album is us figuring out how to work together and recording in that house'.

items.text: Between 2007 and 2011, Adult Swim used several of the album's songs as bumper music, and 'On a Neck, On a Spit' appeared on Reaper, a show on The CW.
items.why: Song appearances: 'From 2007 to 2011, Adult Swim used several songs ... as background music for bumpers'; '"On a Neck, On a Spit" was featured on The CW show Reaper'.

items.text: The first single, 'Knife', came out in May 2007 with an alternate edit of 'Easier' on the other side.
items.why: Release: 'The first single, "Knife", was released on 7-inch vinyl with the exclusive B-side "Easier" (alternate edit) on May 21, 2007'.

items.text: Warp20 (Recreated), a 2009 compilation, included Pivot's take on 'Colorado' and Jamie Lidell's take on 'Little Brother'.
items.why: Release: 'In 2009, the Warp20 (Recreated) compilation featured a cover of "Colorado" by Pivot and "Little Brother" by Jamie Lidell'.

items.text: In 2012, Daniel Rossen recalled that the four of them had been young and eager about making their first record together.
items.why: Release: 'In 2012, ... Daniel Rossen reflected ... "we were so young and so excited about the first record we made as the four of us"'.

items.text: Owen Pallett wrote and played the strings on a tune by Droste's great aunt that the band tried to slow down.
items.why: Recording: '"Marla" itself is actually a song written by Droste's great aunt'; Droste: 'it will be really cool if we slowed it down'; 'The string arrangements on "Marla" were composed and performed by Owen Pallett'. Title matches.

items.text: G. Lucas Crane contributed tapes to this track.
items.why: Personnel: 'G. Lucas Crane – tapes ("Plans")'. Title matches.

missed: That the title names Droste's mother's house where most of it was recorded (Lead), and the Marla backstory (a great aunt who died young in the 1940s, her song found on a family CD). Also the pack's note that the original vinyl plays at 45 RPM.
